note: Let holes be listed from the top-right square to the bottom-left square. Initially their word is D^(m-1)L^(n-1). In a legal 2x2 block, the holes are NE, SE, SW and the NW square is occupied, so the hole path segment is DL; the move replaces SE by NW, changing this segment to LD. Conversely, any DL segment gives exactly the required three holes and an occupied NW square. Any shuffle word with the prescribed counts can be obtained from the initial word by moving its desired leading L across all remaining D letters and recursing. Distinct words give distinct hole sets, so the answer is C(m+n-2,m-1). Edge cases m=1 or n=1 give one word/configuration.
